official.deadline_note: Opening and closing dates are set per participating country; the Australian Embassy in Thailand announced applications for the 2027 intake opened 1 February 2026 and closed 30 April 2026.
official.status_note: Applications for the 2027 Australia Awards Mekong-Australia Partnership Scholarships closed on 30 April 2026 (Thai applicants); the next round is expected in early 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: MAP-funded scholarship benefits remain the same as the Australia Awards program, which includes full tuition fees.
benefits: Return air travel - payment of a single return, economy class airfare to and from Australia, via the most direct route
Establishment allowance - a once only payment as a contribution towards accommodation expenses, text books and study materials
Contribution to Living Expenses (CLE) - a fortnightly contribution to basic living expenses paid at a rate determined by the department
Introductory Academic Program (IAP) - a compulsory program prior to the commencement of formal academic studies covering information on living and studying in Australia
Exclusive access to on-award enrichment through the Mekong-Leaders Network
eligibility: Citizen of Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos or Myanmar
MAP-funded scholarships provide the opportunity to obtain a Master's by research or Master's by coursework qualification at an Australian tertiary institution
From 2026, additional Australia Awards Scholarships are available for Myanmar, funded by the Mekong-Australia Partnership
Scholars must sign a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia and leave Australia for a minimum of two years after completing the scholarship
requirements: Apply through the OASIS portal (oasis.dfat.gov.au) within your country's intake window
application_method: Online application via OASIS, the Australia Awards Scholarships portal
official.application_route: Apply online through OASIS during your country's intake window; Thailand's 2027 intake ran from 1 February to 30 April 2026.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship of Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos or Myanmar required
official.international_eligibility: The award is for citizens of the five Mekong countries studying at Australian institutions
official.duration: The minimum period necessary for the individual to complete the academic program specified by the Australian higher education institution, including any preparatory training
official.description: The Mekong-Australia Partnership (MAP) is a five-year commitment announced at the ASEAN-Australia Special Summit in March 2024, with a second phase of $222.5 million for 2024-2029 that includes additional Master's scholarships per year. MAP-funded scholarships let citizens of Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos and Myanmar undertake a Master's by research or coursework at an Australian tertiary institution, with benefits identical to Australia Awards plus exclusive access to the Mekong-Leaders Network.

verification.notes: dfat.gov.au could not be fetched directly (repeated transport errors), so content was taken from the official DFAT domain's own published listings and the Australian Embassy Thailand government press release; no monetary stipend figure is published on the accessible official pages.

applicant_utility.summary: MAP scholarships are the Mekong-track Australia Awards: full tuition, return economy airfare, an establishment allowance and a fortnightly living contribution, plus Mekong-Leaders Network enrichment, for a Master's by research or coursework in Australia. The 2027 intake closed on 30 April 2026, so build toward the next round. Critically, the two-year home-country return rule is a binding contract term, not an informal expectation.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals from Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos or Myanmar who want a Master's in Australia and can commit to returning home for two years afterwards
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country's specific intake window; dates are set per country and were not simultaneous in the 2027 round
Prepare English proficiency evidence and academic transcripts early, since country rounds run roughly three months
Draft a study plan that connects to MAP priority areas such as water security, climate resilience, transnational crime and economic integration
Decide between coursework and research master's before applying, as the MAP page treats them as distinct qualifications
Be ready to accept the contract conditions, including the minimum two-year departure from Australia after completion
common_rejection_risks: Missing your country's own closing date while watching another country's timeline
Underestimating the two-year home return requirement embedded in the signed contract
Proposing study disconnected from Mekong development priorities in a competitive field-based contest
Assuming Myanmar applicants follow the standard process: from 2026 Myanmar has dedicated MAP-funded places
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award covers tuition, return airfare, an establishment allowance and fortnightly living costs, but visa costs and any expenses beyond the fortnightly contribution are not itemised in the official pages and should be self-funded.
document_audit: The OASIS portal is the only official route; documents requested differ slightly by country intake page, so check your country's instructions rather than a generic checklist
Academic transcripts and English evidence must align with the qualification level claimed in the application
alerts: The 2027 intake closed 30 April 2026; expect the next round around February-April 2027 but verify your country's dates
Australia Awards and MAP-funded places interact: applicants may hold or seek either, so avoid double-counting options
MAP is funded through the second phase (2024-29) of the partnership; continuation beyond that horizon depends on future government decisions
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an OASIS account during your country's intake window, complete the online application with study plan and references, then await selection with your country's intake process.
